summary: Étienne Marc Quatremère was a scholar in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy around 1800 to 1807 and held a post at the Collège de France from 1819 to 1857.

Ñāṇavīra Thera worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, and under traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana. He served in the Royal Artillery from 1939 to 1941 and the Intelligence Corps from 1941 to 1945.

Ösel Tendzin was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fordham University and under Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He was executive vice president at Vajradhatu in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.
Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu from around 1980 to 1986, later held a post there around 1995, and served as an editor of Numen.
